indicators.flag: Client deposits cash into a personal account and then immediately moves it through email money transfers, transfers between accounts, drafts or cheques, or withdraws it, often at multiple financial institutions.
indicators.red_flag: Rapid cash-in / multi-channel fan-out flow-through across institutions
indicators.rationale: Cash-in then immediate fan-out through EMTs / internal transfers / drafts is a classic rapid flow-through pattern fully observable in the bank's own deposit and outbound-payment ledger, yet rarely instrumented as a standing velocity signal — a buildable gap on data already held.

build_logic.logic: Flag a personal account where cash deposits are followed within a short window by outbound EMTs, internal transfers, drafts/cheques or withdrawals totalling a high fraction of the deposited value, escalating when disbursement spreads across multiple channels or destination institutions.
build_logic.source: core deposit ledger joined to outbound payment / EMT rails
build_logic.route: Tier-1 alert → AML analyst review gate

indicators.flag: Client has funds coming in and out of their personal account through email money transfers more quickly than normal.
indicators.red_flag: Accelerated EMT pass-through velocity in and out of a personal account
indicators.rationale: EMT in/out velocity sits entirely in the bank's e-transfer rail data and most institutions already run some pass-through monitoring, but tuning it to a per-client 'faster than normal' baseline is only partially instrumented — an enhancement on data held, not a net-new build.

indicators.flag: Client has funds deposited into his or her personal account in amounts below the reporting threshold from what appear to be multiple third parties located in many parts of a city, broader geographic area or several provinces.
indicators.rationale: Sub-threshold deposits aggregated from many dispersed third parties is textbook structuring, derivable from the bank's own deposit records (amount, originator, location) — a concrete buildable signal on data already held that is seldom run as a standing geographic-dispersion aggregate.

build_logic.logic: Flag a personal account receiving multiple deposits individually below the LCTR reporting threshold from numerous distinct third parties across dispersed geographic locations within the window, where the aggregate materially exceeds the threshold — indicative of structuring to evade reporting.
build_logic.source: core deposit ledger with originator and branch/location attributes
build_logic.route: Tier-1 alert → AML analyst review gate

indicators.flag: Client uses multiple financial institutions; their personal account sees significant cash flow-through; and they carry out little typical banking activity (such as paying household bills).
indicators.red_flag: High cash flow-through, multi-FI, no routine banking activity
indicators.rationale: The bank sees its own cash flow-through and the absence of routine bill-pay activity, but the 'multiple financial institutions' leg needs partial enrichment (counterparty-FI inference from outbound EMT/wire destinations) — instrumentable as an enhancement, not fully closed from a single institution's data.

indicators.flag: Client opens bank accounts for several businesses for no apparent economic reason.
indicators.red_flag: Multiple business accounts with no economic rationale
indicators.rationale: The bank holds its own multi-entity account-opening records, but judging 'no apparent economic reason' across several related businesses needs partial enrichment from beneficial-ownership and KYC linkage; existing onboarding controls can be enhanced rather than rebuilt.

indicators.flag: Client sends or receives virtual currency from an address that is known to be associated with a darknet marketplace
indicators.rationale: Attributing a counterparty virtual-currency address to a darknet marketplace requires external blockchain chain-analytics / address-attribution feeds the bank does not natively hold, so the data must be sourced before any signal is buildable.

indicators.flag: Client sends or receives virtual currency to/from mixing or tumbling services that is unusual for their profile.
indicators.rationale: Mixer/tumbler exposure is partly inferable where the bank already ingests some chain-analytics tagging, but full coverage of decentralised tumbling services needs additional address-label enrichment — buildable once the partial external labels are enriched.

indicators.flag: Client makes wire transfers to or from known cryptocurrency friendly banks.
indicators.rationale: Outbound/inbound wire counterparties are in the bank's own SWIFT/wire data, but flagging 'crypto-friendly' correspondent institutions requires partial enrichment from an external VASP-affiliated-bank reference list — buildable once that classification is enriched onto the wire data.

indicators.flag: Client makes virtual currency or wire transfers to chemical companies located in China, Eastern Europe, or India.
indicators.red_flag: VC / wire transfers to chemical companies in China, Eastern Europe or India
indicators.rationale: Wire/VC transfer destination and counterparty geography are in the bank's payment data, but identifying the counterparty as a chemical company in the named jurisdictions needs partial enrichment from merchant-category / corporate-registry data — buildable once counterparty classification is enriched.

indicators.flag: Client purchases industrial lab equipment with no obvious business need, for example pill presses and industrial pumps.
indicators.red_flag: Pill-press / lab-equipment purchases without business need
indicators.rationale: Identifying a purchase as pill-press / industrial lab equipment requires line-item merchant or invoice detail the bank does not hold for card/wire payments — only the merchant and amount are visible, so the descriptive data must be sourced externally before a signal is buildable.

indicators.flag: Client makes unusual cash deposits to a chemical company’s accounts.
indicators.red_flag: Unusual cash deposits into chemical-company accounts
indicators.rationale: Where the chemical company banks with the same institution, unusual cash deposits to its accounts are visible in the deposit ledger and existing cash-anomaly monitoring applies, but identifying the recipient as a chemical company needs partial business-classification enrichment — an enhancement on partially held data.

indicators.flag: Client makes excessive transactions to payment processing companies that are not commensurate with the subject’s financial profile.
indicators.rationale: Volume and value of outbound payments to identifiable payment processors against the client's expected financial profile are fully derivable from the bank's own transaction ledger and KYC profile — a concrete buildable signal on data already held that is seldom run as a standing processor-concentration check.

build_logic.logic: Flag an account whose aggregate transactions to payment-processing counterparties over the window materially exceed the expected value implied by its KYC/income profile, weighted up by the number of distinct processors, indicating layering through processor rails.
build_logic.source: core transaction ledger joined to counterparty (payment-processor) tagging and KYC profile
build_logic.route: Tier-1 alert → AML analyst review gate

indicators.flag: Client receives email money transfers with references to common street-names for drugs in memo section
indicators.red_flag: Inbound EMT memos referencing drug street-names
indicators.rationale: The EMT memo / reference field is captured in the bank's own e-transfer records, so screening inbound EMT memos against a drug street-name lexicon (fent, fenty, china girl, etc.) is directly buildable on data already held — a high-precision keyword signal that is rarely run as a standing control.

build_logic.logic: Flag inbound email money transfers whose memo/reference field matches a curated drug street-name lexicon (e.g. fent, fenty, china girl, tango, dragon's breath, bean), escalating on repeat hits or multiple distinct senders referencing the same client.
build_logic.source: email-money-transfer records including the memo/reference free-text field
build_logic.route: Tier-1 alert → AML analyst review gate

indicators.flag: Client ships packages under the 1 kg weight.
indicators.rationale: Package weight and shipping behaviour are courier/logistics data the bank does not hold; only a payment to a shipping merchant is visible, so the shipment-level detail must be sourced externally before this indicator is observable.

indicators.flag: Client typically pays for purchases in cash and/or prepaid financial products.
indicators.rationale: Cash usage and the bank's own prepaid-product loads/spend are visible in account data and partially monitored, but a standing 'predominantly cash/prepaid' profile signal is only partially instrumented — an enhancement on data already held.
